sam: Hey folks — seeing a flaky ordering problem in the browser JS SDK streaming path. On slow/throttled networks the final token sometimes arrives before a middle chunk. No errors, connection stays open. :confused:
ingrid: can you share a tiny repro and any logs? Is this via EventSource or fetch+streams? :eyes:
sam: using EventSource in a small sample app. sometimes the console shows seq 1,3,4,2. here's what I log:
```
[15:22:10] seq=1 data="Hello"
[15:22:11] seq=3 data="world"
[15:22:12] seq=4 data="!"
[15:22:15] seq=2 data=", this is"
```
no reconnect error.
raj: sounds like chunk reordering across reconnects or a proxy flush/reassembly issue. are you using last-event-id or any resume token?
andrea: we've observed this when an upstream HTTP/2 proxy splits frames differently during congestion. If the gateway flushes buffers out of order, fragments can be received at the client in a different order. SDKs should defensively reorder by an explicit sequence field if the server can provide one.
sam: SDK's default auto-reconnect will open a new connection while the previous one is draining; maybe two overlapping connections cause replays to interleave. i'm not using last-event-id right now.
ingrid: quick check — can you try setting `enableAutoReconnect: false` and artificially increase `reconnectDelayMs`? if it stops, that narrows it to overlapping connections.
sam: turned off auto reconnect and no out-of-order seen after a minute of throttled testing. looks promising. will try to reproduce with proxy in the loop.
raj: long-term: runtime should emit an `X-Chunk-Seq` header or include a per-chunk monotonic seq in the SSE payload. SDKs should expose options to reorder/dedupe and emit a diagnostic metric when an OOO or duplicate is detected.
andrea: on the runtime side we can add `X-Stream-Session` and `X-Chunk-Seq` on every flush, plus a small checksum per event to detect truncation. that lets clients be robust even across reconnects.
sam: i'll craft a tiny nghttp2-based repro that forces H2 frame splits and add it to the sampleapp tests. if anyone has a recommended test harness for simulating 120kb/s throttling and frame-splits, lmk.
ingrid: QA: include a failing test in sampleapp that runs against a proxy with forced frame-splits so this doesn't regress. also add a smoke test where SDK toggles reorder/dedupe option.
devx-bot: issue created: #4872 "browser-sdk: support out-of-order SSE fragments — reorder/dedupe option + diagnostic metric" https://git.redwood/infra/issues/4872 :robot_face:
sam: thanks all — i'll post the repro and link the PR when ready. :thumbsup:
